context: 6 Outlook There are several ways to further the ideas within this work. In our view, the most promising future direction is to study other quantum proof systems with other multipartite entanglement structures. For example, what is the power of QMAW when the states in W are the Absolutely Maximally Entangled states (see review in [31])? Another direction is to probe the relationship of QMA(2) and purity testing. The proof of Theorem 2 uses two quantum proofs only to implement a purity test. Is there a set of proofs W such that QMAW (2) is strictly more powerful than QMArank1(W) ? If so, there is a setting where unentanglement is useful for something beyond purity testing. A related technical question is whether the continuity condition is necessary to show QMArank1(W) ⊆ QMAW (2). Is there a simple characterization of sets which do not satisfy the continuity condition?

statement: This work also reignites the possibility of showing the power of QMA(2) by proving a gap amplification result (Corollary 8). As a starting point, does the complexity class QMAIS exhibit gap amplification? (Even a small amount of gap amplification implies the existence of new complete problems for QMAIS .) One can ask similar questions about the additional quantum proof systems we discuss, see Section 3.1. Unlike with QMA+ [10], each of these complexity classes demonstrates that unentanglement can be as powerful as the difference between EXP vs. NEXP.
